findings.text: follow-on: the guard passes draw_order explicitly to render() from a test-local constant COMMITTED_DRAW_ORDER='reference-last' (line 24) and never reads render's default (benchmarks/plasma_cell_terminal_state.py line 307) or the argparse default (line 596). The prior review's concern was that a future edit to render()'s default would not fail any test; this guard closes the analytic-column-branch path (the negative control reddens it) but not the default path. A change of the source default to panel-last would leave the test green while the committed CLI figure overpainted. Read the default from the benchmark (or assert it equals the constant) so the two cannot drift.

follow-on: the assertion covers only panels[0] (the analytic panel). The arm panels carry panel-state markers that legitimately differ in position from the reference set, and the committed census for case 0 reads 88 panel-state pixels on panels[1] and panels[2]; those are unasserted. If the node's subject is 'the analytic panel is not overpainted', this is correctly scoped, but a regression on the arm columns would be undetected here.
